segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: At that time Jesus went through the grainfields on the Sabbath. His disciples were hungry, and they began to pluck heads of grain and eat.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the Pharisees saw this, they said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, your disciples are doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry—

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: how he entered the house of God and they ate the loaves of presentation, which neither he nor those with him were permitted to eat, but only the priests?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or have you not read in the Law that on the Sabbath the priests in the temple profane the Sabbath and yet are guiltless?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But I tell you, something greater than the temple is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: If you had known what this means—‘I desire mercy and not sacrifice’—you would not have condemned the guiltless.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For the Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Moving on from there, he went into their synagogue.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And there was a man with a withered hand. They questioned him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Is it permitted to heal on the Sabbath?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: They asked this so that they might accuse him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Which of you, if he has one sheep and it falls into a pit on the Sabbath, will not take hold of it and lift it out?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: How much more valuable, then, is a person than a sheep! So it is permitted to do good on the Sabbath.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then he said to the man,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Stretch out your hand.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: He stretched it out, and it was restored, as sound as the other.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But the Pharisees went out and plotted against him, to destroy him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But Jesus, aware of this, withdrew from there. Many followed him, and he healed them all,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: and he sternly warned them not to make him known,

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: so that what was spoken through Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled:

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: “Here is my servant, whom I have chosen, my beloved, in whom my soul delights. I will put my Spirit upon him, and he will proclaim justice to the Gentiles.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: He will not quarrel or shout, nor will anyone hear his voice in the streets.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: A bruised reed he will not break, and a smoldering wick he will not put out, until he brings justice through to victory.

segments.speaker: scripture
segments.text: And in his name the Gentiles will hope.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then a demon-possessed man who was blind and mute was brought to him, and he healed him, so that the mute man could speak and see.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: All the crowds were amazed and said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Could this perhaps be the Son of David?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But when the Pharisees heard this, they said,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “This man casts out demons only by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Knowing their thoughts, he said to them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Every kingdom divided against itself is laid waste, and no city or household divided against itself will stand.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if Satan casts out Satan, he is divided against himself. How then will his kingdom stand?

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: And if I cast out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons cast them out? For this reason they themselves will be your judges.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: But if it is by the Spirit of God that I cast out demons, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Or how can anyone enter the strong man’s house and carry off his goods unless he first ties up the strong man? Then he will plunder his house.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For this reason I tell you, people will be forgiven every sin and blasphemy, but the blasphemy against the Spirit will not be forgiven.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Whoever speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever speaks against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven, either in this age or in the one to come.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad and its fruit bad, for the tree is known by its fruit.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Offspring of vipers! How can you speak good things when you are evil? For the mouth speaks from the overflow of the heart.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The good person brings good things out of his good storehouse, and the evil person brings evil things out of his evil storehouse.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: I tell you that people will give an account on the day of judgment for every careless word they speak.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For by your words you will be vindicated, and by your words you will be condemned.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Then some of the scribes and Pharisees answered him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Teacher, we want to see a sign from you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he answered them,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “An evil and adulterous generation demands a sign, and no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah the prophet.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For just as Jonah was in the belly of the sea monster three days and three nights, so the Son of Man will be in the heart of the earth three days and three nights.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The men of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they turned back at the preaching of Jonah—and look, something greater than Jonah is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: The queen of the South will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon—and look, something greater than Solomon is here.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: When the unclean spirit goes out of a person, it passes through waterless places seeking rest and does not find it.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then it says, ‘I will return to my house that I came out of.’ And when it arrives, it finds the house empty, swept, and put in order.

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: Then it goes and brings with it seven other spirits more evil than itself, and they go in and live there, and that person’s final condition becomes worse than the first. So it will be for this evil generation as well.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: While he was still speaking to the crowds, his mother and his brothers were standing outside, seeking to speak to him.

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: Someone said to him,

segments.speaker: other
segments.text: “Look, your mother and your brothers are standing outside, seeking to speak to you.”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: But he replied to the one who told him,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Who is my mother, and who are my brothers?”

segments.speaker: narrator
segments.text: And stretching out his hand toward his disciples, he said,

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: “Here are my mother and my brothers!

segments.speaker: Jesus
segments.text: For whoever does the will of my Father in the heavens is my brother and sister and mother.”

notes.note: The Greek verb means simply “it is allowed” and contains no word for law, though the standard in view is the Law of Moses as the Pharisees applied it. Most translations have “lawful.” Plucking grain by hand in someone else’s field was itself allowed (Deuteronomy 23:25); the objection is that doing so on the Sabbath counted as reaping, a form of work.

notes.traditional: the bread of the Presence; the showbread
notes.note: The Greek phrase means loaves “set out” or “presented” before God: twelve loaves laid on a table in the sanctuary each Sabbath and afterward eaten only by the priests (Leviticus 24:5–9). The usual rendering, “bread of the Presence,” translates the Hebrew expression behind the phrase, not the Greek. The story of David is told in 1 Samuel 21:1–6.

The Greek adjective is neuter, “something greater,” not masculine, “someone greater,” and the same is true of the parallel sayings in verses 41 and 42. Some translations nevertheless render “one greater.” The neuter may be an indirect way of pointing to Jesus himself, or it may refer to what is happening through him.

The quotation is Isaiah 42:1–4, in a form that matches neither the Hebrew nor the Septuagint exactly. The Greek word can mean either “servant” or “child.” Isaiah’s Hebrew means “servant,” and that is the usual rendering here, though the wording “my beloved, in whom my soul delights” also recalls the voice at Jesus’ baptism.

One Greek word means both “nations” and, in the plural, the non-Jewish peoples as distinct from Israel; English has to choose. “Gentiles” is the usual rendering here and in verse 21, and “nations” would be equally possible.

The Greek word covers both “judgment” and “justice.” In the Isaiah quotation it stands for a Hebrew word for the right order God establishes, so “justice” is used here and in verse 20. In verses 36, 41 and 42 the same Greek word is rendered “judgment.”

A name for the chief of the demons, identified with Satan in verse 26. Its origin is disputed; it is often connected with the Philistine god called Baal-zebub in 2 Kings 1. The spelling “Beelzebub” in older English Bibles comes from the Latin tradition, not from the Greek manuscripts.

In Semitic idiom “sons” can mean the members of a group, so the phrase refers to people of the Pharisees’ own circle, such as their pupils, who also practiced exorcism. The argument is that the accusation against Jesus would condemn them as well.

This is the verb traditionally rendered “justified.” In a courtroom setting such as this one it means to be declared in the right, the opposite of being condemned, and some translations have “acquitted.” Greek uses a single word-family where English has two (righteous/just, righteousness/justice, justify).

The prophets pictured Israel’s unfaithfulness to God as a wife’s adultery against her husband, as in Hosea, Jeremiah 3 and Ezekiel 16. The word here charges the generation with unfaithfulness to God, not with sexual sin.

The Greek word denotes any huge sea creature and is the word the Septuagint uses in Jonah, where the Hebrew has “a great fish.” “Whale” is too specific. Some modern translations also have “sea monster”; others have “great fish” or “huge fish,” following the Hebrew of Jonah.

“Repent” now suggests mainly feeling sorry, whereas the Greek verb carries the prophets’ call to return to God: a change of direction in mind and conduct. In Jonah 3 the Ninevites “turned from their evil way.” Most translations keep “repented” as an established term understood to include a change of life.

Some important early manuscripts lack this verse. It was probably dropped by accident, since it ends with the same Greek word as verse 46 and verse 48 presupposes it. Some editions of the Greek text print it in brackets.
The Greek is plural, a Semitic turn of phrase characteristic of Matthew that a first-century hearer would have noticed. Most translations flatten it to “heaven.”

candidates.reason: Recurs across the Gospels, Acts and Paul; translations split between “lawful” and “permitted/allowed,” and the choice affects whether readers hear a reference to the Law.
Covers “judgment,” “justice” and “condemnation” across the Gospels, John and the letters; the split by sense needs a fixed rule so chapters agree.
In period usage it means abusive speech against people as well as God; translators vary between “blasphemy” and “slander,” and a rule is needed for when each applies.
Recurs through the Gospels; “demon-possessed,” “demonized” and “afflicted by a demon” are all in use and should not vary between chapters.
Means child, servant or slave by context, and is applied to Jesus in Matthew and Acts 3–4, where “servant” versus “child” is a significant and recurring choice.
